content:
maya: quick spike — I pushed a small prototype for VRAM slicing + swap-reserve to test multi-model co-residency (7B + 13B) on a single A100-80G. seeing intermittent OOMs when long chat sessions blow up KV cache :grimacing:

ryan: what allocation strategy are you testing? arena? cudaMallocManaged?

maya: using our default arena allocator with a soft-reserve shim. key change is a per-model slice + a swap_reserve region we hold pinned as fallback. config attached below.

daria: sharing profiler output — main symptom: p95/p99 latency spikes during background model-swap + KV eviction. flamegraph shows stalls in cuMemcpy and our allocator's free-list searches. KV cache churn leads to repeated small reallocs.

perf-bot: perf job 1769471150 completed — baseline vs prototype: p95 latency +18%, p99 +34% for mixed chat workload (seq len 1024 for 13B, 512 for 7B). Memory headroom reduced by ~4GB under peak.

maya: config snippet:
```json
{
  "vram_slices": [
    {"model": "meta-7b", "slice_gb": 20},
    {"model": "meta-13b", "slice_gb": 48}
  ],
  "swap_reserve_mb": 4096,
  "kv_prewarm": true,
  "workspace_policy": "adaptive",
  "allocator": "arena_shim"
}
```

ryan: thanks. a few hypotheses: 1) our free-list search degenerates with many small frees from KV eviction, 2) swap_reserve pinned pages still cause DMA contention during large memcpy, 3) CUDA stream contention when we do asynchronous pin/unpin + prewarm.

samira: can we try two quick mitigations in prod-like bench: a) enable buffer reuse pool for KV pages (avoid free/alloc churn), b) increase swap_reserve to 8GB to avoid OOM-triggered synchronous swap?

maya: yes. I already implemented buffer-reuse pool (LRU by age) + a background defragmenter that coalesces free blocks during idle periods. toggles: `kv_reuse=true`, `defrag_interval_s=30`.

daria: ran a microbench with kv_reuse=true + defrag_interval_s=30: p95 improved by ~6%, p99 by ~10%. memory fragmentation metric dropped significantly. but overall p99 still worse than baseline because memcpy hotspots persist.

maya: logs from a failing run:
```
[2026-03-16T12:11:23Z] WARN allocator: fragmentation high, free_blocks=312, largest=1.2GB
[2026-03-16T12:11:24Z] ERROR swap: OOM triggered while allocating 2.3GB for kv_cache
[2026-03-16T12:11:24Z] INFO swap: starting async pin/unpin (stream 3)
[2026-03-16T12:11:26Z] WARN memcpy: stalled 180ms (size 1.9GB)
```

ryan: that stalled memcpy is the killer. suggests we need to split large memcpy into chunked pinned async copies to reduce stall. also consider using peer-to-peer copy or memkind to reduce CPU involvement.

samira: for short-term bench, please try chunked-copy patch + increase swap_reserve to 8192MB and rerun co_residency_bench. If that helps, we can add adaptive chunking based on observed memcpy latency.

maya: noted. I'll push branch `vram-slice/chunked-copy` and run bench. tagging @samira for perf run.

deploy-bot: deploy started: vram-slice/chunked-copy -> staging (job 1769471278).

perf-bot: bench run started 1769471290 (co_residency_mixed_chat). Expected duration ~25m.

daria: longer-term items we should track: - allocator free-list O(log n) -> consider segregated-fit buckets, constant-time freelist for small blocks - KV cache eviction policy: soft-evict vs hard-evict prioritizing oldest session tokens - workspace sizing: enforce per-model soft_limit to avoid cross-model steal during spikes

ryan: agree. also we should instrument CUDA memcpy latency by size bucket so we can auto-tune chunk size. add metric `cuda.memcpy.ms[size_bucket]` to console dashboards.

maya: action items:
- maya: push chunked-copy + swap_reserve=8192 and run perf (in progress)
- samira: run experiment set A/B (with/without kv_reuse) and collect flamegraphs
- daria: add memcpy size-bucket metrics + look into segregated freelist prototype
- ryan: prototype async pin/unpin backoff (reduce stream concurrency)

samira: sg, will schedule perf runs and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: bench finished 1769471378 — chunked-copy + 8GB reserve: p95 -7% vs prototype, p99 -15% vs prototype, still +8% p99 vs baseline. fragmentation down, OOMs eliminated in 50 runs.

maya: good signal. next steps: merge buffer-reuse + chunked-copy, open RFC for allocator redesign (segregated-fit), and schedule canary on dedicated nodes.

ryan: sounds good. if perf delta vs baseline persists we'll consider redesigning KV cache to lazy-load hot keys only.

maya: thanks all — will update RFC and post follow-ups.
